analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation, patches and file metadata against the indexed threat scope and selected TB-002/TB-011 details. docs/reports/README.md changes only the date and evidence link; historical entries are surrounding context. configuration.md:1631,1635-1636 distinguishes local assistant discovery from coordinator serving, excludes saved assistant/nativeMember coexistence and describes refusal before stopping workers. These statements do not establish an authorization bypass. Console redaction, owner-only configuration, resource quotations and retirement descriptions were also examined; their implementations are not supplied here.
The new public-model report describes release-carried grants and parity qualifications (2026-10-31-public-cluster-models.md:101-105,122-128), expanding the documented public cluster contract. Its declared M5 Ultra qualifications (:34-40) exceed the directly described pipeline evidence (:68,79-87); its request envelope reaches 1,048,576 tokens and includes sampling, tools and TP media (:109-118), whereas listed measured prompts are much smaller. These are material qualification questions, not proof that runtime admission or coordinator authorization is bypassed.
Integration should inspect ClusterPublicModels.swift, cluster-runtime release generation and grant/qualification consumers to determine whether owner declarations become measured-parity claims, whether exact hardware/mode/schedule/request scopes are enforced, and whether native resource admission independently bounds this envelope. Reconcile release-derived cluster approvals with A-017/T-054's independent build qualification and TB-011/T-052/T-053's current per-connection authorization; model approval must not substitute for identity/privacy gates. Public distributed traffic also warrants checking A-001/TB-007 prompt and media custody, cancellation, tenant-cache isolation and committed-token billing across both ranks. No executable regression is established by these documentation units alone; missing implementation remains a coverage limit, and the release/qualification contract needs further review.
